arxiv-2006-16039.creator: Adam Ó Conghaile, Anuj Dawar
arxiv-2006-16039.description: Abstract . Game comonads, introduced by Abramsky, Dawar and Wang and developed by Abramsky and Shah, give an interesting categorical semantics to some Spoiler-Duplicator games that are common in finite model theory. In particular they expose connections between one-sided and two-sided games, and parameters such as treewidth and treedepth and corresponding notions of decomposition.

arxiv-2105-05842.title: Kernel Thinning
arxiv-2105-05842.creator: \name Raaz Dwivedi \email dwivedi@cornell.edu, \name Lester Mackey \email lmackey@microsoft.com
arxiv-2105-05842.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by \name Raaz Dwivedi \email dwivedi@cornell.edu, \name Lester Mackey \email lmackey@microsoft.com. We introduce kernel thinning, a new procedure for compressing a distribution ℙ \mathbb{P} more effectively than i.i.d. sampling or standard thinning. Given a suitable reproducing kernel 𝐤 ⋆ \mathbf{k}_{\star} and 𝒪 ⁡ ( n 2 ) \mathcal{O}(n^{2}) time, kernel thinning compresses an n n -point approximation to ℙ \mathbb{P} into a n \sqrt{n} -point approximation with comparable worst-case integration error across the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space.

arxiv-2509-24010.title: Search for Distant Hypervelocity Star Candidates Using RR Lyrae Stars
arxiv-2509-24010.creator: Haozhu Fu, Yang Huang, Huawei Zhang
arxiv-2509-24010.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Haozhu Fu, Yang Huang, Huawei Zhang. Hypervelocity stars (HVSs) are stars with velocities exceeding their local escape velocities. Searching for HVSs and studying their origins can be an important way to study the properties of the Milky Way. In this paper, we utilize precise distances for RR Lyrae stars (RRLs) derived from the period-absolute magnitude-metallicity (PMZ) relation, along with proper motions from Gaia DR3, to conduct a large-volume search for HVSs.

pmc-11447236.creator: Nick M Rosenberger, Jeremy A Hemberger, Neal M Williams, Juan Arroyo
pmc-11447236.description: Increasingly frequent heat waves threaten the reproduction of flowering plants; compromising the future persistence, adaptive capacity, and dispersal of wild plant populations, and also the yield of fruit-bearing crop plants. pmc-12563159.title: Counting Cosmic Cycles: Past Big Crunches, Future Recurrence Limits, and the Age of the Quantum Memory Matrix Universe
pmc-12563159.creator: Florian Neukart, Eike Marx, Valerii Vinokur, Kazuharu Bamba
pmc-12563159.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We present a quantitative theory of contraction and expansion cycles within the Quantum Memory Matrix (QMM) cosmology. In this framework, spacetime consists of finite-capacity Hilbert cells that store quantum information. Each non-singular bounce adds a fixed increment of imprint entropy, defined as the cumulative quantum information written irreversibly into the matrix and distinct from coarse-grained thermodynamic entropy, thereby providing an intrinsic, monotonic cycle counter.

pmc-13640174.description: Programmed cell death (PCD) is a fundamental, genetically regulated process crucial for development and homeostasis in multicellular organisms. pmc-13642482.title: High‐Detectivity MOCVD‐Epitaxial h‐BN‐Based Vacuum UV Photodetectors With Pt Nanoparticle‐Engineered Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance Enhancement
pmc-13642482.creator: Zhiwei Gao, Yufan Wei, Weijie Liu, Yongming Zhao, Zhengang Liang, Yuhui Zeng, Zhencheng Li, Yang Peng, Feng Wu, Hao‐Chung Kuo, Jiangnan Dai
pmc-13642482.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study addresses fabrication challenges in hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)‐based vacuum ultraviolet photodetectors (VUV PDs) by implementing platinum nanoparticle (Pt NP)‐induced localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effects to enhance photoresponse characteristics. Size‐controlled Pt NPs (32 nm, 50 nm, 85 nm) are synthesized on metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)‐derived h‐BN surfaces through a cost‐effective dewetting process, with systematic evaluation under 185 nm VUV irradiation.
